pr.title: Run borrowck tests on BIDs and emit tail-expr-drop-order lints for violations
pr.description:
Fix #132861 

r? @nikomatsakis 
cc @compiler-errors 

This patch enlarges the scope where the `tail-expr-drop-order` lint applies, so that all locals involved in tail expressions are inspected. This is necessary to run borrow-checking to capture the cases where it used to compile under Edition 2021 but is not going to pass borrow-checking from Edition 2024 onwards.

The way it works is to inspect each BID against the set of borrows that are still live. If the local involved in BID has a borrow index which happens to be live as well at the location of this BID statement, in the future this will be a borrow-checking violation. The lint will fire in this case.

issues.title: Possible false-negative with `tail-expr-drop-order`
issues.body:
There may be a false-negative with `tail-expr-drop-order`. Reproduction:

1. `curl -L https://crates.io/api/v1/crates/faer-core/0.17.1/download | tar -xz`
2. cd `faer-core-0.17.1`
3. Set up cargo-features and a git repo: `git init . && sed -i '1i cargo-features = ["edition2024"]' Cargo.toml && git add . && git commit -m test`
4. `cargo fix --edition`

On current nightly (2024-11-09), this generates a large number of warnings about tail-expr-drop-order. However, none of them are in the offending function `swap_cols`. Additionally, after #131326, there are no warnings at all.

After switching to 2024, this yields an error:

```
error[E0716]: temporary value dropped while borrowed
     --> src/lib.rs:10425:69
      |
10425 |           $crate::zip::ZipEq::new($crate::zip::ViewMut::view_mut(&mut { $head }), $crate::zipped!($($tail,)*))
      |                                                                       ^^^^^^^^^                              - temporary value is freed at the end of this statement
      |                                                                       |
      |                                                                       creates a temporary value which is freed while still in use
      |
     ::: src/permutation.rs:304:9
      |
304   | /         zipped!(
305   | |             mat_a.const_cast().as_2d_mut(),
306   | |             mat_b.const_cast().as_2d_mut(),
307   | |         )
      | |_________- in this macro invocation
308   |       }
309   |       .for_each(|unzipped!(mut a, mut b)| {
      |        -------- borrow later used by call
      |
      = note: consider using a `let` binding to create a longer lived value
      = note: this error originates in the macro `zipped` (in Nightly builds, run with -Z macro-backtrace for more info)
```

Unfortunately that crate is a maze of types and generics, so it is a bit difficult to minimize.

I'm just assuming this is a tail expression drop change due to the shape of the error.

It does not seem related to the macro, since manually expanding it also does not change anything.

I would expect tail-expr-drop-order to at least warn something here. 

cc @dingxiangfei2009

processing.reason: PR #134523 is a diagnostic/borrowck-analysis fix, not a runtime semantics change. Its only MIR delta is adding a `backward incompatible drop(_4);` `BackwardIncompatibleDropHint` marker to the ElaborateDrops output; that statement is a lint hint and does not change drops, values, or control flow. The new UI tests are compile-fail/check-pass tests for the `tail_expr_drop_order` lint, and the thread-local/recursive-future regressions are check-pass only. The historical false negative is a missing compile-time lint for Edition-2021 code such as `{ String::new().as_str() }.len()`, not a miscompilation: the same program still compiles and runs identically before and after the fix. Consequently, no pair of ordinary Rust functions with identical inputs can expose the historical wrong transformation as differing runtime values. Constructing a boolean model of rustc's BID scheduling/borrowck internals would only test a fabricated reimplementation and would not be a source-grounded historical program-counterexample.

analysis.summary: For ElaborateDrops-visible BID statements, the historical false-negative came from only scheduling BIDs for significant-drop locals and ignoring BID statements during borrowck. The fix schedules BIDs for all relevant tail-expression locals and, during borrowck, checks each BID place against still-live borrows so `tail_expr_drop_order` fires when Edition 2024's earlier drop would be a borrowck violation.
analysis.originalLogic: Historical logic: `schedule_backwards_incompatible_drop` returned early when `!self.local_decls[local].ty.has_significant_drop(self.tcx, self.typing_env())`, so only significant-drop locals became BIDs. During borrowck results visitation, `StatementKind::BackwardIncompatibleDropHint { .. }` was included in a no-op arm with the comment `This do not affect borrowck`. The tail-expression lint therefore did not inspect all BID places and did not run borrowck on BID locations against live borrows.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: The historically incorrect behavior was to gate BID creation on `has_significant_drop` and to ignore BID statements in borrowck. That missed tail-expression temporaries without a `Drop` implementation whose storage is nevertheless borrowed past the Edition 2024 drop point, such as `{ String::new().as_str() }.len()`. The correction is not merely adding diagnostic text: it removes the significant-drop gate so all relevant locals get BIDs, and borrowck checks each BID place against the live-borrow set, using `AccessDepth::Drop` only when the place type `needs_drop`, otherwise `AccessDepth::Shallow(None)`, and then emits the lint for a live non-fake borrow.
analysis.inputDomain: Edition 2021 Rust code covered by the `tail_expr_drop_order` migration lint, where a tail/block temporary has a BID and a borrow of that temporary remains live at the BID location. This especially includes temporaries whose type does NOT need `Drop`, for example `String::new().as_str()` used by `.len()`, `&f()` passed as `&()`, and `&mut || 0` passed as a block argument. Related domain cases include coroutine/async tail expressions with temporary values, recursive boxed futures, and `#[thread_local]` wrapper types with `Drop`. A useful pair differs only in whether the temporary type has a significant destructor/BID gating, exposing the historical false negative.
analysis.trigger: Compiling an Edition 2021 program with `#![deny(tail_expr_drop_order)]` where a tail-expression temporary is borrowed later but its type does not have a significant destructor. The historical implementation fails to emit the lint because no BID is scheduled for that local and borrowck treats BID hints as irrelevant.
preconditions: The source is compiled under Edition 2021 for the future-2024 drop-order lint.
A backwards-incompatible drop (BID) exists for the tail-expression local; after the fix BID scheduling must not require `has_significant_drop`.
At the BID location, a non-fake borrow of the BID place is still live in the borrowck domain, or is reported by Polonius `errors_at`.
The `tail_expr_drop_order` lint is enabled or denied so the diagnostic is observable.
Regression coverage includes non-Drop BID types, thread-local wrapper types, and recursive/opaque async return types to avoid ICEs or normalization cycles.
pitfalls: Do not assume BIDs only matter for types with significant destruction; non-Drop temporaries can still be borrow-live and become Edition 2024 borrowck errors.

Do not treat every BID as a full `Drop` access: non-`needs_drop` BID places are handled with `AccessDepth::Shallow(None)` because otherwise references to thread locals can ICE when borrows behind shared references are not tracked.

Avoid post-analysis normalization for this lint; the patch moves from `ty::TypingEnv::post_analysis` to `ty::TypingEnv::non_body_analysis` and adds a recursive-boxed-future regression for cycle errors.
Skip `BorrowKind::Fake(_)` borrows when checking BIDs so fake borrows do not produce spurious lints.
Reuse the same borrows-in-scope logic as conflict checking, including the Polonius `errors_at` path, so BID checks agree with borrowck.
Stop after the first involving live borrow to avoid duplicate or overlapping lint diagnostics.
analysis.testStrategy: Use an Edition 2021 UI test with `#![deny(tail_expr_drop_order)]` and cases such as `let _ = { String::new().as_str() }.len();`, `f(unsafe { String::new().as_str() }.len());`, a block argument `f({ &mut || 0 })`, and `g({ &f() });`. Check stderr for the lint span, `this temporary value will be dropped at the end of the block`, and borrow-use labels such as `borrow later used by call`. Extend the `ElaborateDrops` MIR expectations to include the additional `backward incompatible drop(_4);` BID. Add check-pass regressions for a recursive boxed future (`Box::pin(test()).await?`) and a `#[thread_local]` wrapper with `Drop`. Also update coroutine/async lint stderr, which gains labels for temporaries like `#3`/`__awaitee`.
evidence: This patch enlarges the scope where the `tail-expr-drop-order` lint applies, so that all locals involved in tail expressions are inspected.

If the local involved in BID has a borrow index which happens to be live as well at the location of this BID statement, in the future this will be a borrow-checking violation. The lint will fire in this case.
// Note that we are *not* gating BIDs here on whether they have significant destructor.
// This is needed because we track the borrows of refs to thread locals,
we'll ICE because we don't track borrows behind shared references.
Make sure we don't cycle error when normalizing types for tail expr drop order lint.
I would expect tail-expr-drop-order to at least warn something here.
